biography: Eduardo Leite, a name synonymous with raw aggression and unwavering determination in the Copa Montana series, hails from the bustling streets of São Paulo, Brazil. Growing up, Eduardo wasn't drawn to the beaches or the football fields like most Brazilian boys; his heart belonged to the roar of engines he'd hear echoing from the nearby Interlagos circuit. His racing journey began humbly, tinkering with go-karts in his uncle's garage, fueled by a burning desire to emulate his idol, Ayrton Senna. A defining moment came during a local karting championship when, after a daring last-lap overtake that left his rival fuming, he realized his aggressive style wasn't just a trait, but a weapon. Now, at 37, Leite is considered to be at the peak of his powers, a seasoned veteran with the hunger of a rookie, consistently challenging for podiums and championships. He's a force to be reckoned with, a reminder that passion and grit can overcome even the most formidable obstacles.
drivingStyle: Leite's driving style is best described as relentless. He attacks every corner with a ferocity that often leaves his competitors scrambling. Known for his late-braking maneuvers and aggressive overtaking, he thrives under pressure and isn't afraid to take risks. Tire management isn't always his forte, often pushing his rubber to the absolute limit in pursuit of a faster lap. He has a knack for sniffing out the smallest of opportunities and exploiting them with ruthless efficiency. Some call it reckless; Leite calls it racing.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Vargas
rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision that cost Vargas a championship.

rivalries.name: Isabela Costa
rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track battle for supremacy, fueled by mutual respect and a desire to be the best.

rivalries.name: Mateus Oliveira
rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities both on and off the track, with Oliveira often criticizing Leite's aggressive driving.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba track just before getting into the car to calm his nerves.
Visits the track alone the night before a race, walking the course to visualize his racing lines.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing the limits, tasting fear, and coming out the other side victorious."
careerHighlight: Winning the Copa Montana championship in 2018 after a nail-biting final race where he overtook two cars on the last lap, securing his place in Brazilian motorsport history.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2020 Interlagos Grand Prix due to a mechanical failure, a race he considered a 'home' victory within reach.
